sentences.zh: 求天正十一月朔入先後曆：

translations.literal: To find the new moon of the eleventh month of the Heavenly Standard entering the advance and retardation table:
translations.idiomatic: To find entry into the advance/retardation table at the Heavenly Standard eleventh-month new moon:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之求月離入曆，求弦、望入曆。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this finding lunar apogee entry into the table, and finding first quarter and full moon entry into the table.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan terms this finding lunar-apogee table entry and finding first-quarter and full-moon table entry.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之推天正經朔入曆。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls it computing the Heavenly Standard canonical new moon's entry into the table.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls it computing the Heavenly Standard canonical new moon's table entry.)

sentences.zh: 以通餘減元積，餘以離總去之為總數；

translations.literal: Subtract the communication remainder from the origin accumulation; remove the total apogee from the remainder to obtain the total count;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the communication remainder from the epoch accumulation; divide the remainder by the apogee total to obtain the cycle count;

sentences.zh: 不盡者，半而進位，以元法收為日，不滿為分。

translations.literal: what remains: halve and carry forward, collect into days by the origin divisor, what does not fill is parts.
translations.idiomatic: for the remainder, round at the half and carry, convert to days using the origin divisor; what does not fill a day counts as parts.

sentences.zh: 如曆中日以下為入先曆；

translations.literal: if it matches the mid-cycle day or below, this is entering the advance table;
translations.idiomatic: If the value is at or below the mid-cycle day, entry is into the advance portion of the table;

sentences.zh: 以上者去之，為入後曆。

translations.literal: if above, remove it—this is entering the retardation table.
translations.idiomatic: if above, subtract the mid-cycle day—entry is into the retardation portion.

sentences.zh: 命日，算外，即得天正十一月朔入先後曆日分。

translations.literal: Name the day; outside the count—this gives the day and parts of the Heavenly Standard eleventh-month new moon entering the advance and retardation table.
translations.idiomatic: Name the day; the count exclusive yields the day and fractional parts for the Heavenly Standard eleventh-month new moon's table entry.

sentences.zh: 累加七日、三千八百二十七分、秒六，盈曆中日及分秒去之，各得次朔、望入先後曆日分。

translations.literal: Accumulate adding 7 days, 3,827 parts, 6 seconds; when full of the mid-cycle day and parts and seconds, remove them—each yields the next new moon and full moon entering the advance and retardation table in day and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly add 7 days, 3,827 parts, and 6 seconds; when the sum exceeds the mid-cycle day and its parts and seconds, subtract the excess—obtaining the table entry in days and parts for each successive new moon and full moon.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》以朔餘減歲積分，以轉分去之，餘以五因之，滿元率收之為度；

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: subtract the new-moon remainder from the year accumulation parts, remove revolution parts; multiply the remainder by five; when full of the origin rate, collect as degrees;
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: subtract the new-moon remainder from the year's accumulated parts and remove revolution parts; multiply the remainder by five; when it fills the origin rate, convert to degrees;

sentences.zh: 以弦策加之，即弦、望所入。

translations.literal: add the quarter-moon arc—this is what the first quarter and full moon enter.
translations.idiomatic: add the quarter-moon increment to obtain first-quarter and full-moon entries.

sentences.zh: 以轉差加之，得後朔曆；

translations.literal: add the revolution discrepancy to obtain the next new moon's table entry;
translations.idiomatic: Add the revolution discrepancy to obtain the following new moon's table entry;

sentences.zh: 累加之，即得弦、望入曆及分。

translations.literal: accumulate adding—this yields first quarter and full moon table entry and parts.
translations.idiomatic: by repeated addition, obtain first-quarter and full-moon table entries and their fractional parts.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》以閏餘減歲積分，餘以曆終分去之，不滿，以宗法除之為日；

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar]: subtract the intercalation remainder from the year accumulation parts; remove calendar terminal parts; what does not fill—divide by the lineage divisor to obtain days;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: subtract the intercalation remainder from the year's accumulated parts and remove calendar terminal parts; divide the remainder by the lineage divisor to obtain days;

sentences.zh: 在象限以下為初限，以上去之，餘為末限，各為入遲疾曆初、末限。）〉

translations.literal: if below the image limit, this is the initial limit; if above, remove it—the remainder is the terminal limit—each is entering the slow-fast table's initial and terminal limits.)
translations.idiomatic: if below the image limit it is the initial limit; if above, subtract the image limit—the remainder is the terminal limit—each marking entry into the initial or terminal portion of the slow-fast table.)

sentences.zh: 又《儀天》法月離先後度數：

translations.literal: Further, the Yitian method for lunar apogee advance and retardation in degrees:
translations.idiomatic: The Yitian method for lunar-apogee advance/retardation in degrees:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之月離陰陽差。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this lunar apogee yin-yang discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this the lunar-apogee yin-yang discrepancy.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求朔弦望昇平定數。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls it finding the fixed leveling numbers for new moon, first quarter, and full moon.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls it finding the fixed leveling values for new moon, first quarter, and full moon.)

sentences.zh: 以月朔、弦、望入曆先後分通減元法，餘進位，下以其日損益率展之，以元法收為分，所得，損益次日下先後積為定數。

translations.literal: For the month's new moon, first quarter, and full moon entering the table, use the advance-retardation parts to reduce the origin divisor entirely; carry the remainder; below, expand by that day's increase-decrease rate; collect into parts by the origin divisor; what is obtained increases or decreases the next day's advance-retardation accumulation below into the fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: For each new moon, first quarter, and full moon table entry, subtract the advance/retardation parts from the origin divisor (carrying remainders); apply that day's increase-decrease rate below; convert to parts using the origin divisor; the result adjusts the next day's advance/retardation accumulation to obtain the fixed value.

sentences.zh: 其七日、十四日，如初數以下者，返減之，以上者去之，餘，返減末數，皆進位，下以損益率展之，各滿末數為分，損益次日下先後積為定數。

translations.literal: For days 7 and 14: if at or below the initial number, reverse and subtract; if above, remove it; the remainder—reverse and subtract the terminal number; all carry forward; below expand by the increase-decrease rate; each when full of the terminal number becomes parts; increase or decrease the next day's advance-retardation accumulation below into the fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: On days 7 and 14: if at or below the initial value, apply reverse subtraction; if above, subtract the initial value and reverse-subtract the remainder from the terminal value (carrying as needed); expand below by the increase-decrease rate; when the result fills the terminal value, convert to parts; adjust the next day's accumulation to obtain the fixed number.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置入曆分，以其日損益率乘之，元率收為分，損益其下陰陽差為定數。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: set the table-entry parts; multiply by that day's increase-decrease rate; collect into parts by the origin rate; increase or decrease the yin-yang discrepancy below into the fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: take the table-entry parts, multiply by that day's increase-decrease rate, convert using the origin rate, and adjust the yin-yang discrepancy below to obtain the fixed value.

sentences.zh: 四七術，如初數已下者，以初率乘之，如初數而一，以損益陰陽差為定數；

translations.literal: Four-seven method: if already at or below the initial number, multiply by the initial rate; divide by the initial number as one; increase or decrease the yin-yang discrepancy into the fixed number;
translations.idiomatic: By the four-seven method: if at or below the initial value, multiply by the initial rate and divide by the initial value; adjust the yin-yang discrepancy to obtain the fixed number;

sentences.zh: 若初數以上者，以初數減之，餘乘末率，末數除之，用減初率，餘加陰陽差，各為定數。）〉

translations.literal: if above the initial number, subtract the initial number; multiply the remainder by the terminal rate; divide by the terminal number; use to subtract the initial rate; add the remainder to the yin-yang discrepancy—each becomes the fixed number.)
translations.idiomatic: if above the initial value, subtract it; multiply the remainder by the terminal rate and divide by the terminal value; subtract from the initial rate and add the remainder to the yin-yang discrepancy—each yielding a fixed number.)

sentences.zh: 朔弦望定日：以日躔、月離先後定數，先加後減朔、弦、望中日，為定日。

translations.literal: Fixed days for new moon, first quarter, and full moon: using the sun's lodge traverse and lunar apogee advance-retardation fixed numbers, add first then subtract from the mean days of new moon, first quarter, and full moon—this is the fixed day.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed new-moon, first-quarter, and full-moon days: apply the solar traverse and lunar-apogee fixed advance/retardation values—add for advance, subtract for retardation—to the mean conjunction days to obtain the fixed dates.

sentences.zh: （二曆法同。）〉

translations.literal: (The two calendars' methods are the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both calendars use the same method.)

sentences.zh: 推定朔弦望日辰七直：以天正所盈之日加定積，

translations.literal: To compute the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon day, chronology, and seven directors: add the Heavenly Standard surplus day to the fixed accumulation,
translations.idiomatic: To determine the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon—day, chronology, and seven directors: add the Heavenly Standard surplus days to the fixed accumulation,

sentences.zh: （視朔、弦、望中日，如入大、小雪氣，即加去年天正所盈之日分；

translations.literal: (Observe the mean days of new moon, first quarter, and full moon: if entering Major or Minor Snow qi, then add last year's Heavenly Standard surplus day and parts;
translations.idiomatic: (If the mean conjunction falls within Major or Minor Snow, add last year's Heavenly Standard surplus in days and parts;

sentences.zh: 若入冬至氣者，即加今年天正所盈之日分。）〉

translations.literal: if entering Winter Solstice qi, then add this year's Heavenly Standard surplus day and parts.)
translations.idiomatic: if within Winter Solstice, add this year's Heavenly Standard surplus.)

sentences.zh: 日滿七十六去之，不滿者，命從金星甲子，算外，即得定朔、弦、望日辰星直也。

translations.literal: When days fill 76, remove them; what does not fill—name from Venus jiazi; outside the count—this gives the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon day, chronology, and star director.
translations.idiomatic: Remove multiples of 76 days; name the remainder from the Venus jiazi cycle; the count exclusive yields the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon—day, chronology, and star director.

sentences.zh: 視朔幹名與後朔同者大，不同者小，其月無中氣者為閏。

translations.literal: If the new moon's stem name matches the following new moon's, it is a large month; if different, a small month; a month without a mid-qi is intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: If a new moon shares the same stem-branch day-name as the next new moon, the month is long; if not, short; any month lacking a mid-qi is intercalary.

sentences.zh: 又視朔所入辰分皆與二分相減，餘二收，用減八分之六，其朔定小餘如此；

translations.literal: Also observe the chronology parts at which the new moon enters; subtract each from the equinox parts; collect the remainder by twos; use to subtract six-eighths—the new moon's fixed small remainder is thus;
translations.idiomatic: Also compare the new moon's chronology parts with the equinox parts; pair remainders and subtract six-eighths accordingly to obtain the fixed small remainder for the new moon;

sentences.zh: 以上者進一日；

translations.literal: if above, advance one day;
translations.idiomatic: if above the threshold, advance the date by one day;

sentences.zh: 朔或有交正見者，其朔不進​​。

translations.literal: if the new moon has a conjunction visible at the proper time, that new moon does not advance.
translations.idiomatic: if the new moon coincides with a visible eclipse at the proper moment, do not advance that new moon.

sentences.zh: 定望小餘在日出分以下者，退一日，若有虧初在辰分以下亦如之。

translations.literal: if the fixed full moon's small remainder is below the sunrise parts, retreat one day; if the eclipse beginning is below the chronology parts, likewise.
translations.idiomatic: If the fixed full moon's small remainder falls below the sunrise fraction, retreat one day; the same applies if the eclipse's first contact falls below the chronology parts.

sentences.zh: （二曆法同。）〉

translations.literal: (The two calendars' methods are the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both calendars use the same method.)

sentences.zh: （《儀天》又有求朔弦望加時月度，置弦、望加時日度，其合朔加時月與太陽同度，其日、度便為月離所次；

translations.literal: (The Yitian [calendar] also has finding the lunar degree at the hour of new moon, first quarter, and full moon: set the sun's degree at the hour of first quarter and full moon; at conjunction the moon at the hour shares the sun's degree—that day and degree is where lunar apogee lodges;
translations.idiomatic: (Yitian also computes the moon's position at the hour of each phase: set the solar degree at first quarter and full moon; at conjunction the moon at that hour shares the sun's degree—that day and degree mark the lunar apogee position;

sentences.zh: 餘加弦、望象度及餘秒，滿黃道宿次去之，即定朔、弦、望加時日、度也。）〉

translations.literal: add the remainder to the first-quarter and full moon image degrees and remainder seconds; when full of the Yellow Path lodge sequence, remove them—this is the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon day and degree at the hour.)
translations.idiomatic: add the remainder to the quarter and full-moon image degrees and seconds; remove full cycles along the Yellow Path lodges—obtaining the fixed day and degree for each phase at its hour.)

sentences.zh: 九道宿度：

translations.literal: Nine-path lodge degrees:
translations.idiomatic: Lodge degrees along the Nine Paths:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》、《儀天》皆謂之月行九道。）〉

translations.literal: (Both the Qianyuan and Yitian [calendars] call this the moon's motion along the nine paths.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both Qianyuan and Yitian call this the moon's Nine-Path motion.)

sentences.zh: 凡合朔所交，冬在陰曆，夏在陽曆，月行青道；

translations.literal: Whenever conjunction occurs: if winter is in the yin calendar and summer in the yang calendar, the moon travels the green path;
translations.idiomatic: At conjunction, when winter falls in the yin half of the year and summer in the yang half, the moon follows the Green Path;

sentences.zh: （冬至、夏至後，青道半交在春分之宿，出黃道東；

translations.literal: (After winter and summer solstices, the green path's half-crossing lodges at the spring equinox lodge, emerging east of the Yellow Path;
translations.idiomatic: (After the solstices, the Green Path's midpoint crosses at the spring-equinox lodge, emerging east of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 立夏、立冬後，青道半交在立春之宿，出黃道東南：至所沖之宿亦如之。）〉

translations.literal: after Start of Summer and Start of Winter, the green path's half-crossing lodges at Start of Spring, emerging southeast of the Yellow Path: reaching the opposite lodge is likewise.)
translations.idiomatic: after Start of Summer and Start of Winter it crosses at Start of Spring, emerging southeast of the ecliptic; at the opposite lodge the pattern is the same.)

sentences.zh: 冬在陽曆，夏在陰曆，月行白道；

translations.literal: if winter is in the yang calendar and summer in the yin calendar, the moon travels the white path;
translations.idiomatic: when winter is in the yang half and summer in the yin half, the moon follows the White Path;

sentences.zh: （冬至、夏至後，白道半交在秋分之宿，出黃道西；

translations.literal: (After winter and summer solstices, the white path's half-crossing lodges at the autumn equinox lodge, emerging west of the Yellow Path;
translations.idiomatic: (After the solstices, the White Path's midpoint crosses at the autumn-equinox lodge, emerging west of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 立冬、立夏后，白道半交在立秋之宿，出黃道西北：至所沖之宿亦如之。）〉

translations.literal: after Start of Winter and Start of Summer, the white path's half-crossing lodges at Start of Autumn, emerging northwest of the Yellow Path: reaching the opposite lodge is likewise.)
translations.idiomatic: after Start of Winter and Start of Summer it crosses at Start of Autumn, emerging northwest of the ecliptic; at the opposite lodge the pattern is the same.)

sentences.zh: 春在陽曆，秋在陰曆，月行朱道；

translations.literal: If spring is in the yang calendar and autumn in the yin calendar, the moon travels the red path;
translations.idiomatic: When spring falls in the yang half and autumn in the yin half, the moon follows the Red Path;

sentences.zh: （春分、秋分後，朱道半交在夏至之宿，出黃道南；

translations.literal: (After the spring and autumn equinoxes, the red path's half-crossing lodges at the summer solstice lodge, emerging south of the Yellow Path;
translations.idiomatic: (After the equinoxes, the Red Path's midpoint crosses at the summer-solstice lodge, emerging south of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 立春、立秋後，朱道半交在立夏之宿，出黃道西南：至所衝之宿亦如之。）〉

translations.literal: after Start of Spring and Start of Autumn, the red path's half-crossing lodges at Start of Summer, emerging southwest of the Yellow Path: reaching the opposite lodge is likewise.)
translations.idiomatic: after Start of Spring and Start of Autumn it crosses at Start of Summer, emerging southwest of the ecliptic; at the opposite lodge the pattern is the same.)

sentences.zh: 春在陰曆，秋在陽曆，月行黑道。

translations.literal: If spring is in the yin calendar and autumn in the yang calendar, the moon travels the black path.
translations.idiomatic: When spring falls in the yin half and autumn in the yang half, the moon follows the Black Path.

sentences.zh: （春分、秋分後，黑道半交在冬至之宿，出黃道北；

translations.literal: (After the spring and autumn equinoxes, the black path's half-crossing lodges at the winter solstice lodge, emerging north of the Yellow Path;
translations.idiomatic: (After the equinoxes, the Black Path's midpoint crosses at the winter-solstice lodge, emerging north of the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 立春、立秋後，黑道半交在立冬之宿，出黃道東北：至所沖之宿亦如之。）〉

translations.literal: after Start of Spring and Start of Autumn, the black path's half-crossing lodges at Start of Winter, emerging northeast of the Yellow Path: reaching the opposite lodge is likewise.)
translations.idiomatic: after Start of Spring and Start of Autumn it crosses at Start of Winter, emerging northeast of the ecliptic; at the opposite lodge the pattern is the same.)

sentences.zh: 四序月離為八節，九道斜正不同，所入七十二候，皆與黃道相會。

translations.literal: The four seasons' lunar apogee form the eight nodes; the nine paths differ in obliquity and alignment; the seventy-two hou they enter all meet the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar apogee through the four seasons yields the eight seasonal nodes; the Nine Paths vary in obliquity; all seventy-two hou they traverse meet the ecliptic.

sentences.zh: 各距交初黃道宿度，每五度為限。

translations.literal: Each is measured from the Yellow Path lodge degree at conjunction's beginning, with every five degrees as one limit.
translations.idiomatic: Each is reckoned from the ecliptic lodge at initial conjunction, in limits of five degrees.

sentences.zh: 初限十二，每限減半，終九限又減盡，距二立之宿減一度少強，卻從減盡起，每限減半，九限終十二而至半交，乃去黃道六度；

translations.literal: The initial limit is twelve; each limit halves; at the ninth limit it is reduced to nothing; from the two establishment lodges subtract one degree and a small excess; then starting from nothing, each limit halves; at the ninth limit it ends at twelve and reaches half-crossing—then six degrees from the Yellow Path;
translations.idiomatic: The first limit is 12, each successive limit halving until the ninth reaches zero; subtract 1° plus a small fraction from the two establishment lodges; then from zero halve again through nine limits until 12 at half-crossing—six degrees from the ecliptic;

sentences.zh: 又自十二，每限減半，終九限又減一度少強，更從減盡起，每限增半，九限終十二，復與日軌相會。

translations.literal: Again from twelve, each limit halves; at the ninth limit subtract one degree and a small excess; again from nothing, each limit increases by half; at the ninth limit it ends at twelve and reunites with the sun's track.
translations.idiomatic: Again from 12, halving through nine limits, then subtracting 1° plus a fraction; from zero, each limit increases by half through nine limits back to 12, reuniting with the solar path.

sentences.zh: 交初、交中、半交，各以限數，遇半倍使，乘限度為泛差。

translations.literal: At conjunction's beginning, middle, and half-crossing, each uses its limit number; when encountering half, double it; multiply by the limit degree to obtain the general difference.
translations.idiomatic: At initial conjunction, mid-conjunction, and half-crossing, apply the limit number—doubling when half—and multiply by the limit in degrees to obtain the general difference.

sentences.zh: 其交中前後各九限，以距二至之宿前後候數乘之，半交前後各九限，各至二分之宿前後候數乘之，皆滿百而一為黃道差。

translations.literal: For the nine limits before and after mid-conjunction, multiply by the hou numbers before and after the lodges of the two solstices; for the nine limits before and after half-crossing, multiply by the hou numbers before and after the equinox lodges—when full of one hundred, divide by one to obtain the Yellow Path difference.
translations.idiomatic: For nine limits before and after mid-conjunction, multiply by the hou counts near the solstice lodges; for nine limits before and after half-crossing, multiply by those near the equinox lodges—divide by 100 to obtain the ecliptic correction.

sentences.zh: 在冬至之宿後，交初前後各九限為減，交中前後各九限為加；

translations.literal: After the winter solstice lodge, the nine limits before and after conjunction's beginning are subtracted; the nine limits before and after mid-conjunction are added;
translations.idiomatic: After the winter-solstice lodge, subtract for the nine limits around initial conjunction and add for those around mid-conjunction;

sentences.zh: 夏至之宿後，交初前後各九限為加，交中前後各九限為減。

translations.literal: After the summer solstice lodge, the nine limits before and after conjunction's beginning are added; the nine limits before and after mid-conjunction are subtracted.
translations.idiomatic: After the summer-solstice lodge, add for the nine limits around initial conjunction and subtract for those around mid-conjunction.

sentences.zh: 大凡月交後為出黃道外，交中後為入黃道內。

translations.literal: In general, after lunar conjunction the moon is outside the Yellow Path; after mid-conjunction it is inside the Yellow Path.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, after conjunction the moon lies outside the ecliptic; after mid-conjunction it lies within it.

sentences.zh: 半交前後各九限，在春分之宿後出黃道外，秋分之宿後入黃道內，皆以差為加；

translations.literal: For the nine limits before and after half-crossing: after the spring equinox lodge, outside the Yellow Path; after the autumn equinox lodge, inside the Yellow Path—all use the difference as addition;
translations.idiomatic: For nine limits around half-crossing: after the spring-equinox lodge, outside the ecliptic; after the autumn-equinox lodge, inside—all corrections are additive;

sentences.zh: 在春分之宿後入黃道內，秋分之宿後出黃道外，皆以差為減。

translations.literal: after the spring equinox lodge, inside the Yellow Path; after the autumn equinox lodge, outside the Yellow Path—all use the difference as subtraction.
translations.idiomatic: after the spring-equinox lodge, inside the ecliptic; after the autumn-equinox lodge, outside—all corrections are subtractive.

sentences.zh: 倍泛差，退一位，

translations.literal: Double the general difference and shift back one place,
translations.idiomatic: Double the general difference and shift one decimal place,

sentences.zh: （遇減，身外除三；

translations.literal: (When subtracting, divide outside the body by three;
translations.idiomatic: (When subtracting, divide the exterior remainder by three;

sentences.zh: 遇加，身外除一。）〉

translations.literal: when adding, divide outside the body by one.)
translations.idiomatic: when adding, divide the exterior remainder by one.)

sentences.zh: 又以黃道差減，為赤道差。

translations.literal: Again subtract to convert the Yellow Path difference into the equatorial difference.
translations.idiomatic: Then convert the ecliptic correction to an equatorial correction by subtraction.

sentences.zh: 交初、交中前後各九限，以差加；

translations.literal: For the nine limits before and after conjunction's beginning and mid-conjunction, add the difference;
translations.idiomatic: For nine limits around initial and mid-conjunction, add the correction;

sentences.zh: 半交前後各九限，皆以差減。

translations.literal: for the nine limits before and after half-crossing, all subtract the difference.
translations.idiomatic: for nine limits around half-crossing, subtract the correction.

sentences.zh: 以黃赤道差減黃道宿度為九道宿度，有餘分就近收為太、半、少之數。

translations.literal: Subtract the Yellow Path and equatorial differences from the Yellow Path lodge degree to obtain the nine-path lodge degree; surplus parts are rounded to large, half, or small numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the ecliptic and equatorial corrections from the ecliptic lodge to obtain the Nine-Path lodge; round fractional remainders to large, half, or small units.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》初數九，每限減一，終於一，限數並同，即八十四除之。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan initial number is nine; each limit subtracts one, ending at one; limit numbers are all the same—divide by eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan's initial value is 9, decreasing by 1 per limit to 1; with identical limit counts, divide by 84.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》初數一百一十七，每限減一十，終於二十七，以一百一除。

translations.literal: The Yitian initial number is 117; each limit subtracts ten, ending at 27—divide by 101.
translations.idiomatic: Yitian's initial value is 117, decreasing by 10 per limit to 27, then divide by 101.

sentences.zh: 二曆皆不身外為法。

translations.literal: Neither calendar uses division outside the body as divisor.
translations.idiomatic: Neither calendar uses exterior-remainder division.

sentences.zh: 初中正交、春秋二分、冬夏二至前後各九限，加減並同《應天》。

translations.literal: For initial, mid, and true conjunction, spring-autumn equinoxes, and winter-summer solstices, the nine limits before and after—all additions and subtractions match the Yingtian [calendar].
translations.idiomatic: Additions and subtractions for nine limits around initial, mid, and true conjunction, both equinoxes, and both solstices match the Yingtian calendar.

sentences.zh: 又《儀天》即除法是九十乘黃道泛差，一百一收為度，乃得月與黃、赤道定差。

translations.literal: Further, the Yitian immediate-division method: multiply the Yellow Path general difference by ninety; collect into degrees by 101—thus obtaining the fixed differences between the moon and the Yellow Path and equator.
translations.idiomatic: Yitian's direct division multiplies the ecliptic general difference by 90 and converts by 101 to degrees, yielding the moon's fixed ecliptic and equatorial corrections.

sentences.zh: 以上入交定月出入各六度相較之差，黃道隨其日行所向，斜正各異，餘皆同《應天》。

translations.literal: The above compares the differences of six degrees each for entering and leaving conjunction in the fixed month; the Yellow Path follows the sun's daily direction—obliquity and alignment differ; the rest all match the Yingtian [calendar].
translations.idiomatic: The above compares six-degree ingress/egress differences at fixed conjunction; the ecliptic follows the sun's daily motion with varying obliquity; otherwise all matches Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》有求定朔望加時入遲疾曆初末限，置經朔、望入遲疾初末限日及餘秒，如求定朔、弦、望法入之，即各得所求。

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] has a method to find the fixed new moon and full moon hour's entry into the slow-fast table's initial and terminal limits: set the mean new moon and full moon's entry days and remainder seconds; apply as in finding fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon—each yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: Yitian provides a method for fixed-phase hours entering the slow-fast table's initial or terminal limits: set the mean-phase entry days and seconds, then apply the fixed new-moon/quarter/full-moon procedure.

sentences.zh: 又求初中正交入曆，置其朔、望加時入遲疾曆初末限日及餘秒，視其日月行入陰陽曆日及餘秒，如近前交者即加，近後交者即返減交中日餘，乃如之，各得初、中、正交入遲疾曆初末限日及餘秒也。

translations.literal: Further, to find initial, mid, and true conjunction table entry: set the new moon and full moon hour's entry into the slow-fast table's initial and terminal limit days and remainder seconds; observe the sun and moon's entry into the yin-yang calendar days and remainder seconds; if nearer the prior conjunction, add; if nearer the following, reverse-subtract the mid-conjunction day remainder—proceed accordingly—each yields initial, mid, and true conjunction entry into the slow-fast table's initial and terminal limit days and remainder seconds.
translations.idiomatic: To find table entry at initial, mid, and true conjunction: set phase-hour entry into slow-fast limits; compare solar and lunar yin-yang calendar entries—add if nearer the prior conjunction, reverse-subtract mid-conjunction remainder if nearer the next—obtaining entry days and seconds for each conjunction type.

sentences.zh: 其加減滿或不足，即進退象限及餘秒，各得所求。

translations.literal: If addition or subtraction fills or is insufficient, advance or retreat the image limit and remainder seconds—each yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: If additions or subtractions overflow or fall short, adjust the image limit and seconds accordingly.

sentences.zh: 又求朔望加時及初、中、正交入遲疾限日入曆積度，各置小餘，以其日曆定分乘之，宗法收之為分，一百一除之為度，以加其日下曆積度，各得所求。

translations.literal: Further, to find new moon and full moon hour and initial, mid, and true conjunction entry into slow-fast limit days and table accumulated degrees: set the small remainder for each; multiply by that day's table fixed parts; collect into parts by the lineage divisor; divide by 101 for degrees; add to that day's table accumulated degrees below—each yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: To find phase-hour and conjunction accumulated degrees in the slow-fast limits: multiply each small remainder by that day's fixed table parts, convert via the lineage divisor and 101 to degrees, and add to the day's accumulated table degrees.

sentences.zh: 又《乾元》、《儀天》有求正交黃道月度，《乾元》元率通定交度及分，以一百二十七乘之，滿九十五而一，進一等，復收為入交度，用減其朔加時日度，即朔前月離正交黃道宿度。

translations.literal: Further, both Qianyuan and Yitian have methods to find true-conjunction Yellow Path lunar degree. Qianyuan: communicate the fixed conjunction degree and parts through the origin rate; multiply by 127; when full of 95, divide by one and advance one rank; collect again as conjunction-entry degree; subtract from the new moon hour's solar degree—this is the lunar apogee true-conjunction Yellow Path lodge degree before the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Both calendars compute true-conjunction ecliptic lunar position. Qianyuan: convert the fixed conjunction degree through the origin rate, multiply by 127, divide by 95 (carrying), reconverting to conjunction-entry degrees; subtract from the new-moon-hour solar degree to obtain pre-conjunction ecliptic lunar apogee position.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》置朔、望及正交曆積度，以少減多，餘為月行去交度及分；

translations.literal: Yitian: set the new moon, full moon, and true conjunction table accumulated degrees; subtract the smaller from the larger—the remainder is the moon's motion's degrees and parts from conjunction;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: set accumulated degrees for new moon, full moon, and true conjunction; subtract the smaller from the larger to obtain the moon's distance from conjunction in degrees and parts;

sentences.zh: 乃視其朔望在交前者加、交後者減朔望加時黃道月度，為初、中、正交黃道月度也。）〉

translations.literal: then observe whether the new moon and full moon are before conjunction—add; after conjunction—subtract from the new moon and full moon hour's Yellow Path lunar degree—this is the initial, mid, and true conjunction Yellow Path lunar degree.)
translations.idiomatic: then add if the phase precedes conjunction or subtract if it follows, from the phase-hour ecliptic lunar degree—yielding initial, mid, and true conjunction ecliptic positions.)

sentences.zh: 九道交初月度：

translations.literal: Nine-path conjunction-beginning lunar degree:
translations.idiomatic: Lunar degree at Nine-Path initial conjunction:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之月離入交九道正交月度、九道朔度。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this lunar apogee entering conjunction nine-path true-conjunction lunar degree and nine-path new moon degree.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan terms this lunar apogee's Nine-Path true-conjunction degree and Nine-Path new-moon degree.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求月離正交九道宿度。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls it finding lunar apogee true-conjunction nine-path lodge degree.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls it finding the Nine-Path lodge at lunar apogee true conjunction.)

sentences.zh: 置月離交初黃道宿度，各以所入限數乘之，

translations.literal: Set the lunar apogee conjunction-beginning Yellow Path lodge degree; each multiply by its entered limit number,
translations.idiomatic: Set the lunar apogee's ecliptic lodge at initial conjunction; multiply each by its limit number,

sentences.zh: （遇半倍使）〉

translations.literal: (when encountering half, double it)
translations.idiomatic: (Double when the limit is half.)

sentences.zh: 如百而一，為泛差；

translations.literal: as one per hundred—this is the general difference;
translations.idiomatic: divide by 100 to obtain the general difference;

sentences.zh: 用求黃、赤二道差，依前法加減之，即月離交初九道宿度。

translations.literal: use to find the Yellow Path and equator differences; add and subtract by the prior method—this is the lunar apogee conjunction-beginning nine-path lodge degree.
translations.idiomatic: compute ecliptic and equatorial corrections and apply the prior addition/subtraction rules to obtain the Nine-Path lodge at initial conjunction.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》以日躔陰陽差陽加陰減，為朔、望常分；

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: using the sun's lodge traverse yin-yang discrepancy—add for yang, subtract for yin—as the mean parts for new moon and full moon;
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: apply the solar traverse yin-yang discrepancy—add for yang, subtract for yin—as mean new-moon and full-moon values;

sentences.zh: 又以所入限率乘，正交黃道宿度相從之，以求黃、赤二道差，如前加減，為月離正交九道宿度；

translations.literal: again multiply by the entered limit rate; the true-conjunction Yellow Path lodge degree follows; find the Yellow Path and equator differences; add and subtract as before—this is the lunar apogee true-conjunction nine-path lodge degree;
translations.idiomatic: multiply by the entered limit rate with the true-conjunction ecliptic lodge; compute ecliptic and equatorial corrections as before to obtain the Nine-Path lodge at true conjunction;

sentences.zh: 以入交定度加而命之，即朔月離宿度。

translations.literal: add the fixed conjunction-entry degree and name it—this is the new moon lunar apogee lodge degree.
translations.idiomatic: add the fixed conjunction-entry degree and name the lodge to obtain the new-moon lunar apogee position.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》置正交月離黃道，以距度下月九道差，宗法乘之，以距度所入限數乘度，餘從之，為總差；

translations.literal: Yitian: set the true-conjunction lunar apogee Yellow Path; multiply the nine-path difference below the distance degree by the lineage divisor; multiply the distance degree's entered limit number by degrees, the remainder following—this is the total difference;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: set true-conjunction ecliptic lunar apogee; multiply the Nine-Path difference below the distance degree by the lineage divisor; multiply the entered limit by degrees with remainder following to obtain the total difference;

sentences.zh: 半而退位，一百一收之，又計冬、夏二至以求度數乘，滿九十而一為度差，依前法加減，為正交月離九道。）〉

translations.literal: halve and shift back one place; collect by 101; again compute winter and summer solstices to find the degree number and multiply; when full of 90, divide by one for the degree difference; add and subtract by the prior method—this is true-conjunction lunar apogee nine-path.)
translations.idiomatic: halve and shift back; convert by 101; compute solstice factors, multiply, divide by 90 for the degree correction; apply prior addition/subtraction rules for true-conjunction Nine-Path lunar apogee.)

sentences.zh: 求九道朔月度：百約月離先後定數，後加先減四十二，用減中盈而從朔日，乃加交初九道宿次，即得所求。

translations.literal: To find the nine-path new moon lunar degree: reduce the lunar apogee advance-retardation fixed number by one hundred; add later and subtract earlier forty-two; use to subtract the mid surplus and follow the new moon day; then add the conjunction-beginning nine-path lodge sequence—this yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: To find the Nine-Path new-moon position: scale the lunar-apogee fixed advance/retardation by 100; add 42 for retardation and subtract for advance; adjust the mid surplus and new-moon day; add the initial-conjunction Nine-Path lodge to obtain the result.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置九道正交之度及分，以入交定度加之，命以九道宿次，即其朔加時月離宿度及分也。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: set the nine-path true-conjunction degree and parts; add the fixed conjunction-entry degree; name by the nine-path lodge sequence—this is the new moon hour's lunar apogee lodge degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: set the Nine-Path true-conjunction degree and parts, add fixed conjunction-entry, and name the Nine-Path lodge for the new-moon hour's lunar apogee position.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》法見下。

translations.literal: The Yitian method is given below.
translations.idiomatic: The Yitian method appears below.

sentences.zh: 《乾元》又有​​定交度，置月離陰陽定數，以七十一乘之，滿九百一除之為分，用陰減陽加常分為度及分。）〉

translations.literal: The Qianyuan [calendar] also has a fixed conjunction degree: set the lunar apogee yin-yang fixed number; multiply by 71; when full of 901, divide for parts; use yin to subtract and yang to add to the mean parts for degree and parts.)
translations.idiomatic: Qianyuan also has a fixed conjunction degree: take the lunar-apogee yin-yang fixed value, multiply by 71, divide by 901 for parts, and subtract for yin or add for yang to the mean parts.)

sentences.zh: 求九道望月度：

translations.literal: To find the nine-path full moon lunar degree:
translations.idiomatic: To find the Nine-Path full-moon position:

sentences.zh: （《儀天》謂之求定朔、望加時日月度。）〉

translations.literal: (The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding the fixed new moon and full moon hour's sun and moon degrees.)
translations.idiomatic: (Yitian calls this finding sun and moon positions at the fixed new-moon and full-moon hours.)

sentences.zh: 以象積加朔九道月度，命以其道，即得所求。

translations.literal: Add the image accumulation to the new moon nine-path lunar degree; name by its path—this yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: Add the image accumulation to the new-moon Nine-Path position and name the lodge along that path.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置朔、望加時日相距之度，以天中度及分加之，為加時象積；

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: set the degrees separating the new moon and full moon hour sun positions; add the celestial mid-degree and parts—this is the hour image accumulation;
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: set the solar separation at new-moon and full-moon hours; add the celestial mid-degree and parts to obtain the hour image accumulation;

sentences.zh: 用加九道朔月度，命以其道宿次去之，即望日月度及分也。

translations.literal: use to add to the new moon nine-path lunar degree; name by its path lodge sequence and remove excess—this is the full moon sun and moon degree and parts.
translations.idiomatic: add to the new-moon Nine-Path lunar position, name the lodge along that path, and remove full cycles to obtain full-moon solar and lunar degrees.

sentences.zh: 自望推朔亦如之。

translations.literal: Deriving new moon from full moon is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Deriving new moon from full moon follows the same procedure.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求定朔望加時九道日度，以其朔、望去交度，交前者減之，交後者加之，滿九道宿度去之，即定朔、望加時九道日度也。

translations.literal: Yitian finds the fixed new moon and full moon hour's nine-path solar degree: using their new moon and full moon degrees from conjunction; before conjunction subtract; after conjunction add; when full of nine-path lodge degrees, remove—this is the fixed new moon and full moon hour's nine-path solar degree.
translations.idiomatic: Yitian finds fixed-phase-hour Nine-Path solar positions: subtract or add the distance from conjunction before or after it, respectively, and remove full Nine-Path lodge cycles.

sentences.zh: 求定朔望加時九道月度，置其日加時九道日度，其合朔者非正交，即日在黃道、月在九道各入宿度，多少不同，考其去極，若應繩準。

translations.literal: To find the fixed new moon and full moon hour's nine-path lunar degree: set that day's hour nine-path solar degree; at conjunction it is not true conjunction—the sun is on the Yellow Path and the moon on the nine paths, each entering lodge degrees, the amounts differing; examine the distance from the pole—as if responding to a plumb line.
translations.idiomatic: To find fixed-phase-hour Nine-Path lunar position: set that hour's Nine-Path solar degree; at conjunction (not true conjunction) the sun lies on the ecliptic and the moon on a Nine Path at different lodge positions; compare polar distances as with a plumb line.

sentences.zh: 故云月與太陽同度也。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said the moon and sun share the same degree.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the text says the moon shares the sun's degree.

sentences.zh: 如求黃道月度法，盈九道宿次去之，各得其日加時九道宿度，自此以後，皆如求黃道月度法入之，依九道宿度行之，各得所求也。）〉

translations.literal: As in finding the Yellow Path lunar degree method: when full of the nine-path lodge sequence, remove it—each obtains that day's hour nine-path lodge degree; from here on, all enter as in finding the Yellow Path lunar degree method; proceed by the nine-path lodge degrees—each yields the desired result.)
translations.idiomatic: As with the ecliptic lunar-degree method: remove full Nine-Path lodge cycles to obtain each hour's Nine-Path position; thereafter apply the ecliptic method along Nine-Path lodges to obtain all desired results.)

sentences.zh: 求晨昏月：

translations.literal: To find the morning and evening moon:
translations.idiomatic: To find the morning and evening moon:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之月離晨昏度。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this lunar apogee morning and evening degree.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this the lunar-apogee morning-and-evening degree.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求晨昏月度。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls it finding the morning and evening lunar degree.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls it finding the morning-and-evening lunar position.)

sentences.zh: 置後曆七日下離分，與其日離分相比較，取多者乘朔、望定分，取少者乘晨昏分，皆滿元法為分，百除為度分，仍相減之，

translations.literal: Set the apogee parts below day 7 of the retardation table; compare with that day's apogee parts; take the greater to multiply the new moon and full moon fixed parts; take the lesser to multiply the morning and evening parts; all when full of the origin divisor become parts; divide by one hundred for degree-parts; still subtract them,
translations.idiomatic: Set apogee parts below day 7 of the retardation table and compare with that day's apogee parts; multiply new-moon/full-moon fixed parts by the greater and morning/evening parts by the lesser; convert via the origin divisor and divide by 100 for degree-parts, then subtract,

sentences.zh: （朔、望度多者為後，少者為前。）〉

translations.literal: (The greater new moon and full moon degree is later; the lesser is earlier.)
translations.idiomatic: (The larger new-moon/full-moon value is after; the smaller is before.)

sentences.zh: 各得晨昏前後度分；

translations.literal: each obtains the morning and evening before and after degree-parts;
translations.idiomatic: each yields the before-and-after morning/evening degree-parts;

sentences.zh: 前加後減朔、望九道月度為晨昏月。

translations.literal: add before and subtract after from the new moon and full moon nine-path lunar degree to obtain the morning and evening moon.
translations.idiomatic: add the 'before' and subtract the 'after' corrections from the new-moon/full-moon Nine-Path position to obtain the morning and evening moon.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置其月離差，在三百九十三以上者，用乘朔、望定分，以下者，只用三百九十三乘，為加時分；

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar]: set its lunar apogee discrepancy; if above 393, use it to multiply the new moon and full moon fixed parts; if below, use only 393 to multiply—this is the hour parts;
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: set the lunar-apogee discrepancy; if above 393, multiply new-moon/full-moon fixed parts by it; if below, use 393—obtaining hour parts;

sentences.zh: 元率除之，進一位，二百九十四收為度；

translations.literal: divide by the origin rate; advance one place; collect into degrees by 294;
translations.idiomatic: divide by the origin rate, shift one place, and convert by 294 to degrees;

sentences.zh: 又以離差乘晨昏分，亦如前收之為度，與加時度相減之，加時度多為後、少為前，即得晨昏前後度及分，加減如《應天》。

translations.literal: again multiply the apogee discrepancy by the morning and evening parts; collect into degrees as before; subtract from the hour degree; if the hour degree is greater it is later, if less it is earlier—this yields the morning and evening before and after degrees and parts; add and subtract as in the Yingtian [calendar].
translations.idiomatic: multiply apogee discrepancy by morning/evening parts and convert as before; compare with the hour degree—greater means 'after,' lesser means 'before'—obtaining before/after degrees; apply additions and subtractions as in Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》以晨昏分減定朔、弦、望小餘為後，不足者，返減之為前，以乘入曆定分，宗法除之，一百一約之為度，乃以前加後減加時月度為晨昏月度。）〉

translations.literal: Yitian: subtract the morning and evening parts from the fixed new moon, first quarter, and full moon small remainder for 'after'; if insufficient, reverse-subtract for 'before'; multiply by the table-entry fixed parts; divide by the lineage divisor; reduce by 101 for degrees; then add before and subtract after from the hour lunar degree to obtain the morning and evening lunar degree.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian: subtract morning/evening parts from fixed-phase small remainders for 'after,' or reverse-subtract for 'before' if insufficient; multiply by table-entry fixed parts, convert via lineage divisor and 101, then adjust the hour lunar position to obtain morning/evening positions.)

sentences.zh: 晨昏象積：

translations.literal: Morning and evening image accumulation:
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening image accumulation:

sentences.zh: （《儀天》謂之求晨昏程積度。）〉

translations.literal: (The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding the morning and evening procedure accumulated degree.)
translations.idiomatic: (Yitian calls this finding the morning-and-evening procedure accumulation.)

sentences.zh: 置加時象積，以前象前後度前減後加，又以後象前後度前加後減，即得所求。

translations.literal: Set the hour image accumulation; with the prior image's before and after degrees, subtract before and add after; again with the following image's before and after degrees, add before and subtract after—this yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: Set the hour image accumulation; subtract 'before' and add 'after' using the prior image's corrections, then add 'before' and subtract 'after' using the following image's corrections.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》法同。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan method is the same.
translations.idiomatic: (The Qianyuan method is identical.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》以所求朔、弦、望加時日度減後朔、弦、望加時日度，餘加弦、望度及餘，為加時程積；

translations.literal: Yitian: subtract the following new moon, first quarter, and full moon hour solar degree from the sought new moon, first quarter, and full moon hour solar degree; add the remainder to the first quarter and full moon degree and remainder—this is the hour procedure accumulation;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: subtract the next phase's hour solar degree from the sought phase's hour solar degree; add the remainder to the quarter/full-moon degree and remainder for the hour procedure accumulation;

sentences.zh: 以所求前後分返其加減，又以後朔、弦、望前後度分依其加減，各為晨昏程積度及餘也。）〉

translations.literal: reverse the addition and subtraction of the sought before and after parts; again apply the following new moon, first quarter, and full moon before and after degree-parts according to their addition and subtraction—each becomes the morning and evening procedure accumulated degree and remainder.)
translations.idiomatic: reverse the before/after additions and subtractions for the sought phase; apply the next phase's before/after corrections similarly—each yielding morning/evening procedure accumulation in degrees and remainder.)

sentences.zh: 求每日晨昏月：

translations.literal: To find the daily morning and evening moon:
translations.idiomatic: To find the daily morning and evening moon:

sentences.zh: （《儀天》謂之求每日入曆定度。）〉

translations.literal: (The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding the daily table-entry fixed degree.)
translations.idiomatic: (Yitian calls this finding the daily fixed table-entry degree.)

sentences.zh: 累計距後象離分，百除為度分，用減晨昏象積為加，不足，返減，以距後象日數除之，為日差；

translations.literal: Accumulate and count the apogee parts from the following image; divide by one hundred for degree-parts; use to subtract from the morning and evening image accumulation for addition; if insufficient, reverse-subtract; divide by the days to the following image—this is the daily difference;
translations.idiomatic: Accumulate apogee parts to the following image, divide by 100 for degree-parts, and subtract from (or reverse-subtract from) the morning/evening image accumulation; divide by days to the following image for the daily difference;

sentences.zh: 用加減每日離分，百除為度分，累加晨昏月，命以九道宿次，即得所求。

translations.literal: use to add and subtract each day's apogee parts; divide by one hundred for degree-parts; accumulate adding to the morning and evening moon; name by the nine-path lodge sequence—this yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: apply daily apogee parts (divided by 100 for degree-parts) to accumulate the morning/evening moon along the Nine-Path lodges.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》法同。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan method is the same.
translations.idiomatic: (The Qianyuan method is identical.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》從所求日累計距後曆每日曆度及分，以減程積為進，不足，返減之，餘為退，以距後朔、弦、望日數均之，進加退減每日曆定度及分，各為每日曆定度及分也。）〉

translations.literal: Yitian: from the sought day accumulate and count each day's table degree and parts from the following table; subtract from the procedure accumulation for advance; if insufficient, reverse-subtract—the remainder is retreat; average by the days to the following new moon, first quarter, and full moon; advance adds and retreat subtracts each day's fixed table degree and parts—each becomes the daily fixed table degree and parts.)
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: from the sought day, accumulate daily table degrees and parts to the following table entry; subtract from procedure accumulation for advance (reverse-subtract if insufficient) for retreat; average over days to the next new moon, first quarter, or full moon; add advance and subtract retreat for each day's fixed table degree and parts.)

sentences.zh: 步晷漏

translations.literal: Procedure for gnomon shadow and clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: Gnomon Shadow and Clepsydra Procedure.

sentences.zh: 求每日晷景去極度晨分：

translations.literal: To find each day's gnomon-shadow departure from the pole degree morning parts:
translations.idiomatic: To find each day's morning parts for gnomon shadow departure from the pole:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之晷景距中度晨分。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this gnomon-shadow distance-from-midheaven morning parts.
translations.idiomatic: (The Qianyuan calendar calls this the morning parts for gnomon shadow distance from midheaven.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》別立法，具後。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] establishes a separate method, given below.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian uses a separate method, given below.)

sentences.zh: 各以氣數相減為分，自雨水後法十六，霜降後法十五，除分為中率，二率相減，為合差；

translations.literal: Each subtract qi numbers from one another for parts; from Rain Water onward use divisor sixteen, from Frost's Descent onward use fifteen; divide parts to obtain the mean rate; subtract the two rates—this is the combined difference;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract qi numbers pairwise for parts; use divisor 16 after Rain Water and 15 after Frost's Descent to get the mean rate; the difference between the two rates is the combined difference;

sentences.zh: 半之，加減中率為初、末率。

translations.literal: halve it; add and subtract from the mean rate for initial and terminal rates.
translations.idiomatic: Halve it and add/subtract from the mean rate to obtain initial and terminal rates.

sentences.zh: （前多者，加為初、減為末；

translations.literal: (Where the prior is greater, add for initial and subtract for terminal;
translations.idiomatic: (If the prior rate is greater, add for the initial rate and subtract for the terminal;

sentences.zh: 前少者，減為初、加為末。）〉

translations.literal: where the prior is lesser, subtract for initial and add for terminal.)
translations.idiomatic: if lesser, subtract for initial and add for terminal.)

sentences.zh: 又以元法除合差，為日差；

translations.literal: again divide the combined difference by the origin divisor—this is the daily difference;
translations.idiomatic: Divide the combined difference by the origin divisor for the daily difference;

sentences.zh: （後多者累益初率，後少者累減初率。）〉

translations.literal: (Where the later is greater, cumulatively increase the initial rate; where the later is lesser, cumulatively decrease the initial rate.)
translations.idiomatic: (If the later rate is greater, cumulatively increase the initial rate; if lesser, cumulatively decrease it.)

sentences.zh: 為每日損益率；

translations.literal: this becomes each day's increase-decrease rate;
translations.idiomatic: yielding each day's increase/decrease rate;

sentences.zh: 以其數累積之，各得諸氣初數也。

translations.literal: accumulate these numbers to obtain each qi's initial number.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulate these values to obtain each qi term's initial number.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》法同。）〉

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan method is the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Qianyuan method is identical.)

sentences.zh: 求昏分：以晨分減元法為昏分。

translations.literal: To find dusk parts: subtract morning parts from the origin divisor—this is dusk parts.
translations.idiomatic: To find dusk parts: subtract morning parts from the origin divisor.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之元率，《儀天》謂之宗法。）〉

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this the origin rate; the Yitian [calendar] calls it the lineage divisor.)
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this the origin rate; Yitian calls it the lineage divisor.)

sentences.zh: 求每日距中度：

translations.literal: To find each day's distance-from-midheaven degree:
translations.idiomatic: To find each day's distance from midheaven:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》同。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] is the same.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan is the same.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求每日距子度。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding each day's distance-from-zi degree.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls this finding each day's distance from the zi meridian.)

sentences.zh: 以百乘晨分，如二千七百三十八為度，不盡，退除為距子度，用減半週天度，餘為距中星度分；

translations.literal: multiply morning parts by one hundred; take as degree with 2,738 as divisor; what remains, retreat-divide for distance-from-zi degree; subtract from half the circuit of heaven degree—the remainder is distance-from-midheaven star degree-parts;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply morning parts by 100; divide by 2,738 for degrees; retreat-divide the remainder for distance-from-zi; subtract from half the circuit-of-heaven degree for distance-from-midheaven star degree-parts;

sentences.zh: 倍距子度分，五等除，為每更度分。

translations.literal: double the distance-from-zi degree-parts; divide in five equal parts—this is each watch's degree-parts.
translations.idiomatic: Double distance-from-zi degree-parts and divide by five for each watch's degree-parts.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》百約晨分，進一位，以三千六百五十三乘，如元率收為度，餘同《應天》。

translations.literal: (Qianyuan: reduce morning parts by one hundred, advance one place, multiply by 3,653, take as degree with the origin rate as divisor; the remainder follows Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: reduce morning parts by 100, advance one decimal place, multiply by 3,653, and divide by the origin rate for degrees; remainder as in Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》置晷漏母，五因，進一位，以一千三百八十二、小分五十五、微分三十五除為度，不盡，以一千三百六十八、小分八十六退除，皆為距子度，餘同《應天》。）〉

translations.literal: Yitian: set the gnomon-clepsydra mother, multiply by five, advance one place; divide for degree with 1,382, minor parts 55, micro-parts 35; what remains, retreat-divide with 1,368, minor parts 86—all as distance-from-zi degree; the remainder follows Yingtian.)
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: set the gnomon-clepsydra mother, multiply by 5 and advance one place; divide by 1,382.55.35 for degrees; retreat-divide remainder by 1,368.86 for distance-from-zi; remainder as in Yingtian.)

sentences.zh: 求每日昏明中星：

translations.literal: To find each day's dusk and dawn culminating stars:
translations.idiomatic: To find each day's dusk and dawn culminating stars:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之昏曉率星。）〉

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this dusk-dawn culminating stars.)
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this dusk-and-dawn culminating stars.)

sentences.zh: 置其日赤道日躔宿次，以距南度分加而命之，即其日昏中星；

translations.literal: Set that day's equator solar progression lodge sequence; add distance-south degree-parts and name—this is that day's dusk culminating star;
translations.idiomatic: Set that day's equatorial solar progression lodge; add distance-south degree-parts and name for the dusk culminating star;

sentences.zh: 以距子度分加之，為夜半中星；

translations.literal: add distance-from-zi degree-parts—this is midnight culminating star;
translations.idiomatic: Add distance-from-zi degree-parts for the midnight culminating star;

sentences.zh: 又加之，為曉中星。

translations.literal: add again—this is dawn culminating star.
translations.idiomatic: Add again for the dawn culminating star.

sentences.zh: （二曆法同。）〉

translations.literal: (The two calendars' methods are the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both calendars use the same method.)

sentences.zh: 求五更中星：置昏中星為初更中星；

translations.literal: To find the five watches' culminating stars: set the dusk culminating star as the first watch culminating star;
translations.idiomatic: To find culminating stars for the five watches: set the dusk star as the first-watch star;

sentences.zh: 以每更度分加之，得二更初中星；

translations.literal: add each watch's degree-parts to obtain the second watch initial culminating star;
translations.idiomatic: Add each watch's degree-parts for the second watch's initial culminating star;

sentences.zh: 又加之，得三更初中星；

translations.literal: add again to obtain the third watch initial culminating star;
translations.idiomatic: Add again for the third watch's initial star;

sentences.zh: 累加之，各得五更初中星所臨。

translations.literal: accumulate adding to obtain each of the five watches' initial culminating stars' positions.
translations.idiomatic: Continue accumulating to obtain the positions for all five watches' initial culminating stars.

sentences.zh: （二曆法同。）〉

translations.literal: (The two calendars' methods are the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (Both calendars use the same method.)

sentences.zh: 求日出入時刻：

translations.literal: To find the sun's rising and setting time and clepsydra marks:
translations.idiomatic: To find the times of sunrise and sunset:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之求晝夜出入辰刻。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this finding day-night rising-setting chen and clepsydra marks.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this finding day-and-night rising-setting chen and marks.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求日出入晨刻及分。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding the sun's rising-setting morning clepsydra marks and parts.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls this finding sunrise/sunset morning marks and parts.)

sentences.zh: 以二百五十加晨減昏為出入分，以八百三十三半除為時，不滿，百除為刻分，命如前，即得所求。

translations.literal: add two hundred fifty to morning and subtract from dusk for rising-setting parts; divide by eight hundred thirty-three and a half for hours; if insufficient, divide by one hundred for clepsydra marks and parts; name as before—this yields the desired result.
translations.idiomatic: Add 250 to morning parts and subtract from dusk for rising-setting parts; divide by 833½ for hours, then by 100 for clepsydra marks and parts; name as before.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》以七十三半加晨減昏為出入分，各以辰法除之。

translations.literal: (Qianyuan: add seventy-three and a half to morning and subtract from dusk for rising-setting parts; each divide by the chen divisor.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: add 73½ to morning and subtract from dusk for rising-setting parts; divide each by the chen divisor.

sentences.zh: 為辰數；

translations.literal: this is the chen count;
translations.idiomatic: This is the chen count;

sentences.zh: 不盡，以五因之，滿刻法為刻，命辰數起子正，算外，即日出入辰刻也。

translations.literal: what remains, multiply by five; what fills the clepsydra divisor becomes clepsydra marks; name chen count from zi midnight, outside the count—this is the sun's rising-setting chen and marks.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply remainder by 5; what fills the clepsydra divisor gives marks; count chen from zi midnight, outside the count, for sunrise/sunset chen and marks.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》置其日晷漏母，以加昏明，餘以三因，滿辰法除為辰數，餘以刻法除為刻，不滿為分，辰數命子正，算外，即日出辰刻及分。

translations.literal: Yitian: set that day's gnomon-clepsydra mother, add to dusk and dawn; multiply the remainder by three; what fills the chen divisor divide for chen count; remainder divide by clepsydra divisor for clepsydra marks, insufficient for parts; name chen from zi midnight, outside the count—this is sunrise chen, marks, and parts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: set that day's gnomon-clepsydra mother and add to dusk/dawn; triple the remainder; divide by chen divisor for chen, by clepsydra divisor for marks (remainder as parts); count from zi midnight for sunrise chen, marks, and parts.

sentences.zh: 乃置日出辰刻及分，以加晝刻及分，滿辰法及分除為辰數，不滿，為入時之刻及分。

translations.literal: Then set sunrise chen, marks, and parts; add day clepsydra marks and parts; what fills chen divisor and parts divide for chen count; what remains is the setting-time clepsydra marks and parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set sunrise chen, marks, and parts; add day marks and parts; divide by chen divisor for chen count; remainder gives sunset marks and parts.

sentences.zh: 乃置其辰數，命子正，算外，即得日入辰刻及分。）〉

translations.literal: Then set its chen count; name from zi midnight, outside the count—this yields sunset chen, marks, and parts.)
translations.idiomatic: Name chen from zi midnight, outside the count, for sunset chen, marks, and parts.)

sentences.zh: 晝夜分：

translations.literal: Day-night parts:
translations.idiomatic: Day and night parts:

sentences.zh: （《乾元》謂之晝夜刻。

translations.literal: (The Qianyuan [calendar] calls this day-night clepsydra marks.
translations.idiomatic: (Qianyuan calls this day-and-night clepsydra marks.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》謂之求每日夜半定漏、求每日晝夜刻。）〉

translations.literal: The Yitian [calendar] calls this finding each day's midnight fixed clepsydra and finding each day's day-night clepsydra marks.)
translations.idiomatic: Yitian calls this finding each day's midnight fixed clepsydra and day-night marks.)

sentences.zh: 倍日出分，為夜分；

translations.literal: double the sunrise parts—this is night parts;
translations.idiomatic: Double sunrise parts for night parts;

sentences.zh: 減元法，為晝分；

translations.literal: subtract from the origin divisor—this is day parts;
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from the origin divisor for day parts;

sentences.zh: 百約，為盡夜分。

translations.literal: reduce by one hundred—this is the full night parts.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce by 100 for total night parts.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置日入分，以日出分減之為晝分，以減元率為夜分，以五因之，以刻法除為晝夜刻分。

translations.literal: (Qianyuan: set sunset parts; subtract sunrise parts for day parts; subtract from the origin rate for night parts; multiply by five; divide by clepsydra divisor for day-night clepsydra marks and parts.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: set sunset parts; subtract sunrise for day parts; subtract from origin rate for night parts; multiply by 5 and divide by clepsydra divisor for day-night marks.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》先求夜半定漏，置其日晷漏母，以刻法除之為刻，不滿，三因為分，為夜半定漏及分。

translations.literal: Yitian: first find midnight fixed clepsydra; set that day's gnomon-clepsydra mother; divide by clepsydra divisor for clepsydra marks, insufficient multiply by three for parts—this is midnight fixed clepsydra and parts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: first find midnight fixed clepsydra from that day's gnomon-clepsydra mother; divide by clepsydra divisor for marks, triple remainder for parts.

sentences.zh: 置夜半定漏刻及分，倍之，其分滿刻法為刻，不滿為分，即得夜刻及分。

translations.idiomatic: Summer-solstice upper limit equals winter-solstice lower limit; summer-solstice lower equals winter-solstice upper.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求每日陽城晷景常數：置入冬、夏二至後求日數及分，以所入象日數下盈縮分盈減縮加之為其日定積，又以減其象小餘為夜半定積及分。

translations.literal: Yitian: to find each day's Yangcheng gnomon-shadow constant: set the days and parts sought after winter and summer solstices; with the image days entered, surplus subtract and deficit add the image's surplus-deficit parts for that day's fixed accumulation; again subtract the image's minor remainder for midnight fixed accumulation and parts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for each day's Yangcheng gnomon-shadow constant: set days and parts after solstices; apply surplus-deficit of the entered image for the day's fixed accumulation; subtract the image's minor remainder for midnight fixed accumulation.

sentences.zh: 又隔位除一，用若夜半定積及分在二至上限以下者，為入上限之數；

translations.literal: Again divide by one at every other position; if midnight fixed accumulation and parts are below the solstice upper limit, this is the number entering the upper limit;
translations.idiomatic: Divide by one at alternate positions; if midnight fixed accumulation is below the solstice upper limit, that is the upper-limit entry;

sentences.zh: 以上者，以返減前限日及約餘，為入下限日及分。

translations.literal: if above, reverse-subtract from prior-limit days and reduced remainder for lower-limit entry days and parts.
translations.idiomatic: If above, reverse-subtract from prior-limit days and reduced remainder for lower-limit entry.

sentences.zh: 若冬至後上限、夏至後下限，以十四乘之，所得，以減上下限差分，為定差法；

translations.literal: If after winter solstice upper limit or after summer solstice lower limit, multiply by fourteen; subtract the product from upper-lower limit difference parts for the fixed-difference divisor;
translations.idiomatic: For winter-solstice upper or summer-solstice lower limit, multiply by 14 and subtract from upper-lower limit difference for the fixed-difference divisor;

sentences.zh: 以所入上下限日數再乘之，所得，滿一百萬為尺，不滿為寸及分，以減冬至晷影，餘為其日中晷景常數也。

translations.literal: multiply again by the upper-lower limit days entered; what fills one million is chi, insufficient is cun and parts; subtract from winter-solstice gnomon shadow—the remainder is that day's mid-gnomon-shadow constant.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply again by entered limit days; divide by 1,000,000 for chi (remainder cun and parts); subtract from winter-solstice shadow for that day's mid-gnomon constant.

sentences.zh: 若夏至後上限、冬至後下限，以三十五乘之，以上下差分為定法；

translations.literal: If after summer solstice upper limit or after winter solstice lower limit, multiply by thirty-five; use upper-lower difference parts as the fixed divisor;
translations.idiomatic: For summer-solstice upper or winter-solstice lower limit, multiply by 35 and use upper-lower difference as the fixed divisor;

sentences.zh: 以入上下限日數再乘之，退一等，滿一百萬為尺，不滿尺為寸及分，用加夏至晷景，即得其日中晷景常數。

translations.literal: multiply again by the upper-lower limit days entered; retreat one place; what fills one million is chi, insufficient chi is cun and parts; add to summer-solstice gnomon shadow—this yields that day mid-gnomon-shadow constant.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply again by entered limit days, retreat one place; divide by 1,000,000 for chi (remainder cun and parts); add to summer-solstice shadow for that day mid-gnomon constant.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求晷景每日損益差：以其日晷景與次日晷景相減，其日景長於次日晷影為損，短於次日晷景為益。

translations.literal: Yitian: to find each day gnomon-shadow daily increase-decrease difference: subtract that day gnomon shadow from the next day gnomon shadow; if that day shadow is longer than the next day gnomon shadow, it is decrease; if shorter than the next day gnomon shadow, it is increase.
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for each day gnomon-shadow increase-decrease difference: subtract next day shadow from this day; longer shadow than the next day is decrease, shorter is increase.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求陽城中晷景定數：置五千分，以其日晷景定數損益差乘之，所得，以萬約之為分，冬至後用減，夏至後用加；

translations.literal: Yitian: to find Yangcheng mid-gnomon-shadow fixed number: set five thousand parts; multiply by that day gnomon-shadow fixed-number increase-decrease difference; divide the product by ten thousand for parts; after winter solstice use to subtract, after summer solstice use to add;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for Yangcheng mid-gnomon fixed number: set 5,000 parts; multiply by that day shadow fixed-number difference; divide by 10,000 for parts; subtract after winter solstice, add after summer solstice;

sentences.zh: 冬至一日有減無加，夏至一日有加無減。

translations.literal: On the day of winter solstice there is decrease without increase; on the day of summer solstice there is increase without decrease.
translations.idiomatic: On winter-solstice day only decrease applies; on summer-solstice day only increase.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求晷漏損益度入前後限數：置入冬至後來日數，在前限以下者為損；

translations.literal: Yitian: to find gnomon-clepsydra increase-decrease degree entry into prior-posterior limit numbers: set the days elapsed after winter solstice; if below the prior limit, it is decrease;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for gnomon-clepsydra increase-decrease entry into prior/posterior limits: set days after winter solstice; below the prior limit is decrease;

sentences.zh: 以上者，減去前限，餘為入後限日數者為益。

translations.literal: if above, subtract the prior limit—the remainder as days entering the posterior limit is increase.
translations.idiomatic: If above, subtract the prior limit; the remainder as posterior-limit entry days is increase.

sentences.zh: 若算立成，自冬至後一日，日加滿初象，即加象下約餘，為一象之數。

translations.literal: If using ready-made tables, from the day after winter solstice, daily add until the first image fills, then add the image reduced remainder—this is one image number.
translations.idiomatic: With ready-made tables, from the day after winter solstice add daily until the first image fills, then add the image reduced remainder for one image count.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》求每日晷漏損益數：置入前後限損益日數及分，如初象以下為在上限；

translations.literal: Yitian: to find each day gnomon-clepsydra increase-decrease number: set the prior-posterior limit increase-decrease days and parts; if below the first image, it is in the upper limit;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for each day gnomon-clepsydra increase-decrease number: set prior/posterior limit increase-decrease days and parts; below the first image is upper limit;

sentences.zh: 以上者，返減前限，餘為下限，皆自相乘之，其分半以下乘，半以上收之；

translations.literal: if above, reverse-subtract the prior limit—the remainder is lower limit; each self-multiplies; parts half and below multiply, half and above collect;
translations.idiomatic: If above, reverse-subtract the prior limit for lower limit; self-multiply each; multiply parts at half or below, collect at half or above;

sentences.zh: 以一百通日，內其分，乃乘之；

translations.literal: convert the day with one hundred, include its parts, then multiply;
translations.idiomatic: Convert the day with 100, include parts, then multiply;

sentences.zh: 所得，在冬至後初象、夏至後次象，以升法除之。

translations.literal: the product, in winter-solstice first image or summer-solstice second image, divide by the ascending divisor.
translations.idiomatic: For winter-solstice first image or summer-solstice second image, divide the product by the ascending divisor.

sentences.zh: 若冬至後次象、夏至後初象，以平法除之；

translations.literal: if winter-solstice second image or summer-solstice first image, divide by the leveling divisor;
translations.idiomatic: For winter-solstice second image or summer-solstice first image, divide by the leveling divisor;

sentences.zh: 皆為分，不滿，退除為小分；

translations.literal: each becomes parts; if insufficient, retreat-divide for minor parts;
translations.idiomatic: Yield parts; retreat-divide remainder for minor parts;

sentences.zh: 所得，置於上位，又別置五百五分於下，以上減下，以下乘上；

sentences.zh: 置去極度分，與九十一度三千八百四十五相減，餘者為赤道內外度分。

translations.idiomatic: In Yitian, for dusk parts and distance-from-noon parts: set day origin parts; subtract that day gnomon-clepsydra mother for dusk parts.

sentences.zh: 又以其日晷漏母減五千五十分，餘者為其日距午分。

sentences.zh: 置其朔入曆盈、縮日及分，如四十五日以上、一百三十七日以下，皆以一千五百乘，為泛差；

translations.literal: Set its new-moon entry-into-table surplus and deficit days and parts; if like forty-five days and above, one hundred thirty-seven days and below, each multiply by one thousand five hundred—for general difference;
translations.idiomatic: Set new-moon surplus/deficit table entry days and parts; if 45–137 days, multiply by 1,500 for general difference;

sentences.zh: 如四十五日以下，返減之，餘為初限日，一百三十七日以上者減去之，餘為末限日及分，以六十七乘，半之，用減泛差，以乘距午分，以元法收為黃道定分；

translations.literal: if like forty-five days and below, reverse-subtract—the remainder is initial-limit days; if one hundred thirty-seven days and above, subtract it—the remainder is terminal-limit days and parts; multiply by sixty-seven, halve, use to subtract general difference; multiply by distance-from-noon parts; collect by origin divisor for Yellow Path fixed parts;

sentences.zh: 入盈，以定分午前內減外加、午後內加外減；

translations.literal: entering surplus: with fixed parts, before noon inner subtract outer add, after noon inner add outer subtract;

sentences.zh: 入縮，以定分午前內加外減，午後內減外加。

translations.literal: entering deficit: with fixed parts, before noon inner add outer subtract, after noon inner subtract outer add.

sentences.zh: （《乾元》置入氣日，以距冬至之氣，以十五乘之，以所入氣日通之，以一百八十二日以下為入陽曆，以上者去之，為入陰曆。

translations.literal: (Qianyuan: set entry-into-qi day; with qi distance from winter solstice, multiply by fifteen; convert with entered qi day; one hundred eighty-two days and below is entry into yang table, above remove—for entry into yin table.
translations.idiomatic: (In Qianyuan: set entry-into-qi day, multiply qi distance from winter solstice by 15, convert with entered qi day; ≤182 days is yang table entry, above is yin table entry.

sentences.zh: 置入曆分，在四十五日以下，以三十七乘，五除，退一等，為泛差；

translations.literal: Set entry-into-table parts; if forty-five days and below, multiply by thirty-seven, divide by five, retreat one place—for general difference;
translations.idiomatic: Set table-entry parts; if ≤45 days, ×37, ÷5, retreat one place for general difference;

sentences.zh: 在四十五日以上、一百三十七日以下，只用三十三、秒三十為泛差；

translations.literal: if forty-five days and above, one hundred thirty-seven days and below, use only thirty-three, seconds thirty for general difference;
translations.idiomatic: If 45–137 days, use only 33, 30 seconds for general difference;

sentences.zh: 一百三十七以上者去之，餘以三十七乘，五除，退一位，用減三十三、秒三十為泛差；

translations.literal: if one hundred thirty-seven and above, remove it; remainder multiply by thirty-seven, divide by five, retreat one place; use to subtract from thirty-three, seconds thirty for general difference;
translations.idiomatic: If ≥137 days, remove; remainder ×37, ÷5, retreat one place; subtract from 33, 30 seconds for general difference;

translations.literal: each multiply by distance-from-noon parts for gnomon difference.
translations.idiomatic: Each × distance-from-noon parts for gnomon difference.

sentences.zh: 《儀天》二至後日益差至立春、立秋，得一百一十三、小分六十二半，立夏、立冬後每日損，以宗法乘之；

translations.literal: Yitian: from solstice daily increase difference until spring establishment and autumn establishment, obtaining one hundred thirteen, minor parts sixty-two and a half; after summer establishment and winter establishment daily decrease; multiply by lineage divisor;
translations.idiomatic: In Yitian: from solstice daily increase to spring/autumn establishment reaches 113, 62½ minor parts; after summer/winter establishment daily decrease; multiply by lineage divisor;

sentences.zh: 冬至、立冬後三氣用四十四萬二千三百八十四，夏至、立夏后各三氣用二十七萬九千八百五十八除，為食差；

translations.literal: after winter solstice and winter establishment three qi use four hundred forty-two thousand three hundred eighty-four; after summer solstice and summer establishment each three qi use two hundred seventy-nine thousand eight hundred fifty-eight divide—for eclipse difference;
translations.idiomatic: After winter solstice/winter establishment three qi divide by 442,384; after summer solstice/summer establishment three qi divide by 279,858 for eclipse difference;

sentences.zh: 以食甚距午正刻乘其日食差，為定差；

translations.literal: multiply that day eclipse difference by eclipse greatest distance-from-noon true clepsydra marks—for fixed difference;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply that day eclipse difference by greatest-eclipse distance-from-noon true marks for fixed difference;

sentences.zh: 冬至後，甚在午正東，陰減陽加；

translations.literal: After winter solstice, if greatest at true noon east, yin subtract yang add;
translations.idiomatic: After winter solstice: if greatest is east of true noon, yin subtract and yang add;

sentences.zh: 甚在午正西，陰加陽減；

translations.literal: if greatest at true noon west, yin add yang subtract;
translations.idiomatic: If west of true noon, yin add and yang subtract;

sentences.zh: 夏至後即返此；

translations.literal: after summer solstice reverse this;
translations.idiomatic: After summer solstice reverse these rules;

sentences.zh: 立冬初日後，每氣益差二十、秒四十四，至冬至初日加六十二、秒三十二；

translations.literal: after winter establishment first day, each qi increase difference twenty, seconds forty-four, until winter solstice first day add sixty-two, seconds thirty-two;

sentences.zh: 置入盈縮曆日及分，如九十一日以下，返減之，為初限日；

translations.idiomatic: Set surplus/deficit table entry days and parts; if ≤91 days, reverse-subtract for initial-limit days;

sentences.zh: 以上者，用減一百八十二日半，餘為末限日及分；

translations.literal: if above, subtract from one hundred eighty-two days and a half—the remainder is terminal-limit days and parts;
translations.idiomatic: If above, subtract from 182½ days for terminal-limit days and parts;

sentences.zh: 四因之，用減三百七十四，為泛差；

translations.literal: multiply by four; use to subtract three hundred seventy-four—for general difference;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by 4 and subtract from 374 for general difference;

translations.literal: multiply by distance-from-midheaven parts; take one per half day parts; use to subtract general difference—for equator fixed parts;
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by distance-from-midheaven parts, divide by half day-parts, subtract from general difference for equator fixed parts;

sentences.zh: 盈初縮末內減外加、縮初盈末內加外減。

translations.literal: surplus initial deficit terminal: inner subtract outer add; deficit initial surplus terminal: inner add outer subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus-initial/deficit-terminal: inner subtract, outer add; deficit-initial/surplus-terminal: inner add, outer subtract.
